For Immediate Release

 

 

SPAR Group, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results

Second Consecutive Quarter of Profitability with Improving Gross Margins

Expands Growth Pipeline with New Multi-Year Retail Partner Agreement

 

CHARLOTTE, NC, November 13, 2026 – SPAR Group, Inc. (OTCQB: SGRP) (“SGRP”, and together with its subsidiaries, “SPAR,” “SPAR Group” or the “Company”), an innovative services company offering comprehensive merchandising and sales solutions for retailers and brands throughout the United States and Canada, today reported financial results for the periods ended September 30, 2026.

 

William Linnane, President and Chief Executive Officer of SPAR Group, commented, “I am pleased with our progress in returning to profitability for the second consecutive quarter. Although lower remodel activity year over year impacted revenue in the U.S., sales growth in Canada and our continued focus on higher-quality revenue drove continued profitability, resulting in positive net income, stronger gross margins year on year, and a 47% increase in Adjusted EBITDA on a year-to-date basis. Importantly, after quarter-end, we signed a three-year services agreement with a national retailer for merchandising, store remodeling, and temporary labor services, beginning in 2027. We are building a business with greater earnings consistency, stronger customer relationships, an enhanced go to market approach, improved in store execution and improved operating leverage. As we look to quarter four 2026, and to full year 2027, we will leverage improved operating performance to generate consistent cash flow and to improve financial stability, leading to a strengthened balance sheet over time. This is a key strategic focus. The third quarter represents another significant step forward in SPAR’s transformation but there is more to do as we remain focused on increasing profitability, creating free cashflow and reducing debt.”

 

“At the same time, we continue to invest in strategic initiatives designed to accelerate future growth. Our strategic partnership with ReposiTrak combines advanced retail technology and data intelligence with SPAR’s nationwide execution platform to create a differentiated solution that helps retailers and consumer goods vendors to drive sales, improve on-shelf availability, increase labor efficiency, and enhance the consumer experience. Initial results from our joint go-to-market Touchless Retail approach have been very positive. More broadly, we expect that our work with ReposiTrak will lead to new go-to-market opportunities and will result in an improved operating model." concluded Linnane.

 

Steven Hennen, Chief Financial Officer of SPAR Group, commented, “Our third quarter financial performance reflects continued progress against our strategic and financial objectives. Gross margin expanded to 18.9%, notwithstanding lower U.S. revenue, while disciplined cost management drove SG&A expenses down 39% from the prior year. As a result, we reported positive net income for the second consecutive quarter and generated $1.4 million in Adjusted EBITDA in the quarter. These results demonstrate the earnings potential of our merchandising-focused business model and the benefits of actions taken over the past year to improve operational efficiency and streamline the organization.”

 

“We believe our focus on recurring merchandising revenue, disciplined expense management, and operational execution positions SPAR to continue enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder returns,” concluded Hennen.

 

1

 

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

 

 

●

Net revenues were $33.5 million, down 19.0% year-over-year.

 

●

Gross Margin was 18.9% of sales, up from 18.6% of sales in the prior year, driven by the mix of services in the U.S.

 

●

Selling, general and administrative expenses declined 39.0% year-over-year to $5.6 million, reflecting benefits from cost reduction initiatives and organizational restructuring.

 

●

Net income was $50 thousand, or $0.00 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of ($8.8) million, or ($0.37) per diluted share, in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted diluted income per common share was $0.01 compared to adjusted diluted loss per share of $(0.17) in the prior year period.

 

●

Adjusted EBITDA was $1.4 million, compared to the prior year of $90 thousand.

 

 

Nine Months Ended 2026 Highlights

 

 

●

Net revenues were $101 million, down 11.5% year-over-year.

 

●

Gross Margin was 21.3% of sales, from 21.1% of sales in the prior year.

 

●

Selling, general and administrative expenses declined 19.2% year-over-year to $18.6 million, reflecting benefits from cost reduction initiatives and organizational restructuring.

 

●

Net loss was ($94) thousand, or ($0.00) per diluted share, compared to a net loss of ($8.3) million, or ($0.35) per diluted share, in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted diluted income per share was $0.04 compared to adjusted diluted loss per share of ($0.14) in the prior year period.

 

●

Adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million, compared to the prior year of $2.9 million, up 47.3% year on year

 

Financial Position as of September 30, 2026

 

The Company ended the quarter with $4.7 million of cash and cash equivalents. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used by operating activities was $7.2 million, driven by working capital intensity from the acceleration of growth initiatives.

 

2026 Financial Guidance

 

We are adjusting our full-year 2026 financial outlook to reflect our continued focus on higher-margin merchandising services and our current expectations for lower remodel activity this year. In addition, the guidance reflects some projects which have moved from 2026 to 2027, and a slowdown in certain retail sector capital spends as 2026 progressed. While this impacts revenue expectations, the gross margin enhancements year on year and the cost base reductions support our objective of improving earnings quality, profitability, and long-term shareholder value:

 

 

●

Net revenues in the range of $125 to $130 million compared to 2025 Net revenues of $136 million for the U.S. and Canada.

 

●

Gross margins of 20.0%-22.0%, versus 2025 Gross margin of 15.9% for the U.S. and Canada.

 

●

Selling, general, and administrative costs, excluding unusual items, of $23.5 to $25.0 million, versus 2025 of $32.2 million.

 

 

About SPAR Group, Inc.

 

SPAR Group is an innovative services company offering comprehensive merchandising, marketing and distribution solutions to retailers and brands throughout the United States and Canada. We provide resources and analytics that improve brand experiences and transform retail spaces. We offer a unique combination of scale and flexibility with a passion for client results that separates us from the competition. For more information, please visit the SPAR Group’s website at http://www.sparinc.com.

Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Financial Measures

 

Non-GAAP net income attributable to SPAR Group and related per share amounts represent net income attributable to SPAR Group adjusted for the removal of a one-time positive adjustment. Adjusted EBITDA represents net income (loss) before, as applicable from time to time, (i) depreciation and amortization of long-lived assets, (ii) interest expense (iii) income tax expense, (iv) restructuring, (v) impairment, (vi) nonrecurring legal settlement costs and associated legal expenses unrelated to the Company's core operations, (vii) special items as determined by management, and (viii) review of strategic alternatives. These metrics are supplemental measures of our operating performance that are neither required by, nor presented in accordance with, GAAP. These measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative to performance measures derived in accordance with GAAP as an indicator of our operating performance. We present Adjusted net income (loss) attributable to SPAR Group and per share amounts, and Adjusted EBITDA because management uses these measures as key performance indicators, and we believe that securities analysts, investors and others use these measures to evaluate companies in our industry. Our calculation of these measures may not be comparable to similarly named measures reported by other companies.
